glossary.name: Revenue
glossary.text: Sales recognised during the reporting period. It is not the same as cash received, profit or a company’s stock-market value.

glossary.name: Operating income & margin
glossary.text: Operating income is revenue after operating costs and expenses, before items such as interest and taxes. Operating margin divides operating income by revenue.

glossary.name: GAAP net income
glossary.text: Profit or loss under generally accepted accounting principles, after non-operating items and taxes. Tesla’s figures here are attributable to common stockholders; SpaceX uses its reported consolidated net income.

glossary.name: Operating cash flow
glossary.text: Cash generated or used by operating activities during the stated period. Working-capital timing means it can differ substantially from net income.

glossary.name: Capital expenditure
glossary.text: Spending on long-lived assets, using each issuer’s stated definition. It is a cash-use measure rather than a deduction from revenue in the same period.

glossary.name: Free cash flow
glossary.text: Often calculated as operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Definitions can differ. The Tesla bridge uses Tesla’s reported measure; the SpaceX bridge labels an editorial subtraction and its nine-month period.

glossary.name: Adjusted EBITDA
glossary.text: A non-GAAP measure with issuer-specific adjustments. It does not equal net income or free cash flow. Read the issuer’s reconciliation before comparing companies.

glossary.name: Share price & market capitalisation
glossary.text: A share price is the price of one share. Market capitalisation uses a relevant share count as well. Comparing two share prices alone does not compare the size or value of the businesses.
